verdict.rationale: Reflect's homepage calls it 'an open-source note-taking app' and invites users to 'Explore the code on GitHub', so its own materials say the source is readable. However, no license is named and no repository URL is given, so the 'open license' part of the story is unconfirmed. Confidence is low because these two homepage lines sit beside a pack otherwise describing a hosted, end-to-end-encrypted service, and no independent source corroborates open-sourcing. missing for 10: named open license (e.g., MIT/AGPL), a specific repository link, evidence of which components are open (clients vs. server), independent or hands-on corroboration that the code is public.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
